items.title: McNeal Breaux Interview, 1958-11-24
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Nickerson and his brother... That was Nickerson. [INTERVIEWEE] I don't know what Jimmy Jolison... I didn't know him too well.

ctx.x: During the Depression generally? Yeah. Down a quarter was the top price, most places. Yeah. I mean, now and then you get a special affair for two dollars a night. Oh, I know you know Sam Nicholson. Oh, yeah. Sam and his brother. Well, uh... Get the whole player. Phillip. Phillip. Phillip. Well, listen, it's just, those Nicholson, I mean, I knew them not too very well, but they related to Albert Nichols. No, no. Because Albert Nicholson was... That was Nicholson. Oh, Nicholson. Sam Nicholson. And, uh... His…
Nickerson and his brother, he did talk with his college man. That was Nickerson.

I don't know what Jimmy Jolison. I don't know, I don't know, uh, Mac Neal, the Sonny South, Mac Neal, Sonny South. He was a fine trumpet man. He had a nice band too. I used to, I used to hear that most like the, uh, the San Jacinto quote. Bob lines? No, I didn't know him too well.
